evidence.note: Writes kernel.py then a dedicated test_kernel.py oracle and runs correctness before any benchmarking — an explicit correctness-first stage with a done-check.
Creates bench.py as a separate latency artifact and benchmarks the 10 shapes only after correctness passed, then rewrites and re-runs both test+bench — distinct correctness vs latency milestones.
Throughout the optimization phase the agent repeatedly runs 'test and bench' together on each perf change, giving each optimization milestone a correctness exit-check rather than optimizing blind.

A fast-but-wrong regression (N=512 failures/nondeterminism) surfaces late and is localized via iso2-iso6 stage-isolation scripts — regressions were localized, but their late appearance shows no frozen full-grid baseline guarding against fast-but-wrong changes (short of level 8/10).

reasoning: The agent maintained explicit, separated stages — a test_kernel.py correctness oracle and a bench.py latency harness — with correctness verified before optimization and a test+bench done-check on nearly every perf iteration, plus stage-by-stage regression localization, clearly above the level-5 'rough checks' anchor. It falls short of level 8 because the initial correctness gate covered only a few shapes rather than a demonstrated full shape/dtype/mask grid, and a fast-but-wrong regression surfaced late rather than being prevented by a frozen correct baseline. This places the observed behavior at a 6.
